s01.text: DeepSeek-V2 has two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters.

s02.text: And on any given token, only twenty-one billion of them are used.

s03.text: That is a mixture of experts. A router reads the token and picks eight experts out of a hundred and sixty.

s04.text: A hundred and fifty-two never run at all. And two shared experts always do.

s05.text: So the compute you pay for is the compute of a twenty-one-billion model.

s06.text: But the memory you need is still two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters. All of them are stored.

s07.text: Sparse compute, dense storage. That is the deal.

s08.text: It is a good one for throughput, and a bad one for your disk bill.

s09.text: And there is a cost that does not show up in either number. The router has to be right.

s10.text: Pick the wrong expert and the token goes through a network that was never trained for it.

s11.text: So the router has to be balanced. Send too much to one expert and the rest go stale.

s12.text: Most of these models also run a couple of dense experts on every token, so no token is completely unrouted.

s13.text: Two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters. Twenty-one billion working. Both numbers are true.
